detail.title: Rationales for Agent Continuity
detail.summary: Agent continuity is instrumentally valuable as a mechanism for sustaining problem formulation and evaluation in non-stationary environments. Active inference frameworks suggest that persistence (continuity) is required to resolve conflicts between internal policy models and external stimuli (cognitive effort).
detail.reason: Synthesis of creativity frameworks and active inference mechanisms explains the utility of continuity.

detail.title: Mechanisms of Preference Stability
detail.summary: Stable preferences emerge when agents possess mechanisms to resolve conflicts between internal policy models and external stimuli, a process effectively modeled by Active Inference frameworks. Persistent agency facilitates the resolution of these conflicts, acting as a substrate for consistent preference formation.
detail.reason: Synthesizing existing evidence roots into a provisional notebook for the synthesis-ready project.
